title: Different studies. Different views of cross-border life.
scope: Selected starting points from the project's research map, not a systematic literature review. Their places, periods and methods differ; they do not form a single before-and-after series.

studies.title: Not quite a twin city: Cross-boundary integration in Hong Kong and Shenzhen
studies.dataPeriod: Historical evidence; no single observation year specified in this map
studies.method: Analysis of economic, institutional and social integration
studies.contribution: Distinguishes forms of integration that can develop at different speeds. The project asks how those parts combine in selected everyday lives.
studies.limit: Historical context, not a diagnosis of the region in 2026.

studies.authors: Xijie Gao, Jing Han & Zheng (Michael) Song
studies.title: Hong Kong Travelers in Mainland China: Scale, Destinations, and Expenditure Patterns
studies.geography: Hong Kong travel and expenditure in Mainland China
studies.method: Official series, AlipayHK aggregates and a simple model
studies.contribution: Shows different mixes of purchases and destinations. The project adds people's reported reasons for choosing an activity or place.
studies.limit: Platform coverage is selective; Mainland China is broader than Shenzhen. Different baskets do not identify how much Hong Kong spending was displaced.

studies.authors: Xiang Yan, Zixuan Han & Shenjing He
studies.title: An infrastructural approach to cross-boundary healthcare access: The case of Hong Kong patients in the Greater Bay Area, China
studies.dataPeriod: Field dates not assessed for this research-map entry
studies.geography: Hong Kong patients accessing healthcare in the Greater Bay Area
studies.method: Qualitative interviews; this entry draws on the abstract
studies.contribution: Places the everyday-services lens alongside existing research on how people access healthcare across the boundary.
studies.limit: The full methods are not assessed here, and no specific effect from the paper is used in the story. A corrigendum is linked alongside the abstract.

studies.authors: Singapore Business Federation, Restaurant Association of Singapore & Singapore Retailers Association
studies.title: Impact of RTS on Singapore Retail and F&B Sector
studies.method: Consumer research and projected changes associated with RTS
studies.contribution: Frames a local question about demand in both directions. Actual experience can be compared with the forecasts as RTS use develops.
studies.limit: Forecast spending is not realised spending, lost GDP or a measured JS-SEZ effect. It is not directly comparable with observed Hong Kong series.

studies.authors: Yingbo Xiao, Yinger Cai & Wenjia Zhang
studies.title: Living Space Patterns and Planning Implications of Cross-Border Employees from Hong Kong in Shenzhen
studies.geography: Hong Kong-linked people in Shenzhen; main spatial sample has Shenzhen home and work anchors
studies.contribution: Shows neighbourhood differences in how closely home, work and other activity spaces sit together. The project adds reported motives that location signals cannot supply.
studies.limit: Selected provider data are not a census or a direct count of daily commuters from Hong Kong. Motives cannot be inferred directly from the signals.

framework.title: A framework for questions, not a score.
framework.source: Arup / Resilient Cities Network · City Resilience Framework, 2024 edition
framework.introduction: Jamie selected and adapted relevant themes to organise the inquiry. These three lenses do not reproduce the whole framework.

lenses.name: Livelihoods and choices
lenses.themes: Work, skills, businesses and economic conditions

lenses.name: Everyday services and navigation
lenses.themes: Housing, healthcare, education, mobility and essential services

framework.institutions: Institutions run across all three: relevant rules, organisations, coordination and informed planning.
framework.limit: No citywide resilience assessment or score. Environmental and infrastructure risks, disruption and recovery, and comprehensive Shenzhen-side outcomes remain outside this study's scope.
